About

Hi, I'm Pascale. Nice to meet you!

I'm a real estate consultant with Engel & Völkers in Lisbon. Belgian by birth, citizen of the world at heart: I lived in Brazil and Kenya, first came to Portugal as an Erasmus student twenty years ago, and finally made Lisbon my home. I know how it feels to start a new life in another country.

When I bought my own apartment, I visited almost 40 properties, so I know what makes a buyer say yes. Today I live in Lapa and specialise in the Estrela parish and the neighbourhoods around it. I love it here: the river, the light, and the beach just 25 minutes away.

People like working with me because of who I am. I only work on things I truly believe in, but once I do, I keep going until we reach the goal. Personal, structured and honest: a clear plan, regular updates and no surprises.

Common questions

Seller questions

What owners ask me most

Do I have to sign an exclusive contract?

No. Exclusive is never mandatory: you always choose. I'll explain the advantages so you can decide. With an exclusive, your home appears with one price and one beautiful presentation, I can invest in professional photos and real marketing, and you have one contact with a weekly update. And exclusive doesn't mean fewer buyers: I share my listings with other agencies, so their buyers can visit too.

Who decides the price?

You do, always. I look at recent sales and current listings of similar homes nearby, and at your home's condition, floor, light and outdoor space. I explain everything in a written market study, so you can choose the asking price with real facts. The same goes for offers: I advise you, but you decide the final sale price.

What do you need from me to get started?

For your free market study, your caderneta predial, your energy certificate if possible, and a short visit to your home. Before your home goes online, I need all the documents: caderneta predial, certidão permanente, energy certificate, and the ID and NIF of every owner. I help you request anything that's missing. Once everything is complete, we sign the mediation contract, and the photo shoot follows the same or the next day.

When do I pay your commission?

Only when your home is sold. The commission is agreed upfront in the mediation contract and is paid half at the CPCV and half at the escritura.

How long does a sale take?

Finding the right buyer depends on price, condition and demand. With the right price and a complete file, homes in and around Estrela usually find a buyer within a few months. After that, everything goes quickly in Portugal: the promissory contract (CPCV) is usually signed within one to three weeks, and the deed often follows one to two months later. That's why I prepare your documents from the start, so nothing slows the sale down.

My focus area

Estrela

Green, calm and classic. Life here turns around the Jardim da Estrela and the white dome of the basilica, with tram 28 rattling past. Buyers come for the elegant early-20th-century buildings, high ceilings and wooden floors, and for a real neighbourhood feel close to the centre.

Jardim da EstrelaBasílica da EstrelaRua de São Bento and its antique shopsTram 28

Pascale's tip

Walk the side streets around the garden. Some of the most beautiful buildings are just one block away from the main roads.

My home base · Estrela parish

Lapa

Lisbon's embassy quarter and one of its most prestigious addresses. Quiet, sloping streets with palacetes, gardens behind high walls and, from the upper floors, wide views over the Tagus. Homes here are rare on the market and buyers are often ready to wait for the right one.

My favourite places

My Lisbon

Where I eat, move, listen to music and take care of myself. The places I recommend to friends and clients who are new here.

Mexican fusion

Maiz do Mar

Right next door to me. Chef Rodrigo's Mexican fusion kitchen: very fresh ingredients, dishes full of flavour and always such a friendly team. Tiny, but so cosy, and I'm always happy to be there.

Google MapsInstagram
Sweet treat

O Melhor Bolo de Chocolate do Mundo

My favourite chocolate cake for years, long before I got to know Carlos, the man behind it. Now we're friends, and I'm still just as addicted. It's right across from the Mercado de Campo de Ourique, and there's also a little kiosk on Avenida da Liberdade, the one I go to most because it's near the office. Try it once and you'll understand the name.

Google Maps
Yoga

Baraza Yoga

After almost fifteen years of yoga, this is where I come back to myself. Very qualified teachers and a welcoming atmosphere. When I was looking for my own home, living close to this studio was one of my must-haves.

Google MapsInstagram
Move

mvmt.studio

Right in front of the Museu de Arte Antiga, and where I step out of my comfort zone. Great teachers, a really welcoming atmosphere and lots of different classes. I often leave proud, and just as often stiff the next day.

Curious? Try a free class with me →
Google MapsInstagram
Lunch by the water

Último Porto

The place I'd almost rather keep secret. Full of locals, and you get there in a funny way: by crossing a little bridge into the port. Amazing charcoal-grilled fish, right by the water. It can get busy, but that's part of the charm.

Google MapsInstagram
Garden lunch

Clube de Jornalistas

A hidden garden restaurant in an old house, with a lovely terrace. I’d wanted to go for a long time and finally went recently: very flavourful dishes, and you never overeat, which I love.

Google Maps
Wind down

Garden of the Museu de Arte Antiga

My favourite place to wind down. Many people don't know the museum has such a lovely garden, with one of the best views over the river and the bridge. The renovation is almost finished, and I can't wait for it to reopen.

Google MapsInstagram
Concerts

Museu do Oriente

In a former port warehouse by the river in Alcântara, the museum often has lovely concerts at very fair prices: piano, jazz and music from all over the world. An easy cultural evening, close to home.

Google MapsInstagram
Sunrise, by the river…
Run

From my home to Belém and back

I regularly run along the river at sunrise, from my home to Belém and back. The light on the water and the bridge is magic. And a little secret most people don't know: you can run laps around the port, between the boats and the containers.

Last Sunday of the month…
Music

Lisbon Living Room Sessions

On the last Sunday of every month you'll find me at a living room concert, in someone's home and often right here in the neighbourhood. I discover new places and new people, and every time I fall in love with Lisbon, and with life, all over again.

Common questions

Buyer questions

What buyers ask me most

How do I prepare financially to buy?

Know your total budget, including IMT, stamp duty, deed and registration fees on top of the price. If you need a mortgage, get a pre-approval before you visit; non-residents usually need a larger down payment. I help you prepare and connect you with trusted mortgage brokers, so contact me early.

Can I buy from abroad?

Yes. You need a Portuguese tax number (NIF) and a Portuguese bank account. I can introduce you to a trusted lawyer who helps with both and can even sign for you with a power of attorney, so you don't need to fly in for every step.

How long does buying take?

Faster than in many other countries, and faster than most people expect. My own purchase went very quickly too. Once your offer is accepted, the promissory contract (CPCV) is usually signed within one to three weeks, with a deposit of at least 10% of the price, sometimes more. The deed often follows one to two months later. A cash purchase can be done in about four to six weeks in total; with a mortgage, count on two to three months. That's why I help you prepare your documents and financing before you make an offer.

How much can I borrow?

For your own home, Portuguese banks usually lend up to 90% of the value, for a second home or an investment up to 80%. So you need savings for the rest of the price, plus the purchase taxes and fees. How much exactly depends on your income: a broker can tell you in one conversation.

Can I get a mortgage if I don't live in Portugal?

Yes, several Portuguese banks lend to non-residents. They usually ask for a bigger down payment and more documents, so start early, before you make an offer.

Does the mortgage broker cost me anything?

No. The broker I work with compares several banks for you, at no cost to you. Ask me and I'll introduce you personally.

Common questions

Frequently asked questions

The questions sellers and buyers ask me most. Can't find yours? Send me a message, I reply within one working day.

SellingBuyingMortgage

Selling

Do I have to sign an exclusive contract?

No. Exclusive is never mandatory: you always choose. I'll explain the advantages so you can decide. With an exclusive, your home appears with one price and one beautiful presentation, I can invest in professional photos and real marketing, and you have one contact with a weekly update. And exclusive doesn't mean fewer buyers: I share my listings with other agencies, so their buyers can visit too.

Do you only sell luxury homes?

No. Engel & Völkers has a premium image, but premium is about the service, not the price. I work with all kinds of homes, from studios to large family apartments, as long as I believe I can sell them well for you.

Who decides the price?

You do, always. I look at recent sales and current listings of similar homes nearby, and at your home's condition, floor, light and outdoor space. I explain everything in a written market study, so you can choose the asking price with real facts. The same goes for offers: I advise you, but you decide the final sale price.

What do you need from me to get started?

For your free market study, your caderneta predial, your energy certificate if possible, and a short visit to your home. Before your home goes online, I need all the documents: caderneta predial, certidão permanente, energy certificate, and the ID and NIF of every owner. I help you request anything that's missing. Once everything is complete, we sign the mediation contract, and the photo shoot follows the same or the next day.

Why do you ask for so many documents?

Because the law requires it. In Portugal, every real estate agent must identify both the seller and the buyer and complete an anti-money laundering form. This is mandatory for every sale. I'll ask for your ID (Cartão de Cidadão or passport) and NIF, and for buyers also where the funds come from. Checking everything early protects you and avoids problems later, at the promissory contract or the deed.

Do I need an energy certificate?

Yes. A valid certificado energético is required to advertise a property in Portugal. If you don't have one, I can put you in touch with a certified expert.

When do I pay your commission?

Only when your home is sold. The commission is agreed upfront in the mediation contract and is paid half at the CPCV and half at the escritura.

How long does a sale take?

Finding the right buyer depends on price, condition and demand. With the right price and a complete file, homes in and around Estrela usually find a buyer within a few months. After that, everything goes quickly in Portugal: the promissory contract (CPCV) is usually signed within one to three weeks, and the deed often follows one to two months later. That's why I prepare your documents from the start, so nothing slows the sale down.

Buying

How do I prepare financially to buy?

Know your total budget, including IMT, stamp duty, deed and registration fees on top of the price. If you need a mortgage, get a pre-approval before you visit; non-residents usually need a larger down payment. I help you prepare and connect you with trusted mortgage brokers, so contact me early.

Can I buy from abroad?

Yes. You need a Portuguese tax number (NIF) and a Portuguese bank account. I can introduce you to a trusted lawyer who helps with both and can even sign for you with a power of attorney, so you don't need to fly in for every step.

How long does buying take?

Faster than in many other countries, and faster than most people expect. My own purchase went very quickly too. Once your offer is accepted, the promissory contract (CPCV) is usually signed within one to three weeks, with a deposit of at least 10% of the price, sometimes more. The deed often follows one to two months later. A cash purchase can be done in about four to six weeks in total; with a mortgage, count on two to three months. That's why I help you prepare your documents and financing before you make an offer.

Looking for a home outside Lisbon?

My focus is Estrela and the neighbourhoods around it. For a small number of buyers I also search myself in Costa da Caparica, Arrábida & Sesimbra, Comporta and the Alentejo. Beyond Lisbon → Looking on the Silver Coast, in Cascais, the Algarve or Porto? I'll introduce you to a trusted Engel & Völkers colleague there.

Mortgage

How much can I borrow?

For your own home, Portuguese banks usually lend up to 90% of the value, for a second home or an investment up to 80%. So you need savings for the rest of the price, plus the purchase taxes and fees. How much exactly depends on your income: a broker can tell you in one conversation.

Can I get a mortgage if I don't live in Portugal?

Yes, several Portuguese banks lend to non-residents. They usually ask for a bigger down payment and more documents, so start early, before you make an offer.

Why get a pre-approval before visiting?

You know exactly how much you can spend, and sellers take your offer seriously.

Does the mortgage broker cost me anything?

No. The broker I work with compares several banks for you, at no cost to you. Ask me and I'll introduce you personally.

Privacy

Privacy policy

Last updated: November 2026. I keep this short and clear: what I collect, why, and what you can ask me at any time.

Who I am

This website belongs to Pascale Lepoutre, real estate consultant working with EV MMC Portugal – Mediação Imobiliária, Unipessoal Lda., Engel & Völkers Lisboa, AMI 15208. For any question about your data, write to pascale.lepoutre@engelvoelkers.com.

What I collect

Only what you send me yourself through the forms or by WhatsApp: your name, phone number, email, the address or street of your property, what you are looking for, such as budget, areas and timing, and any documents you choose to upload, such as your caderneta predial or energy certificate.

Why I use it

  • To answer your question and prepare your free market study.
  • To search for homes that fit what you are looking for.
  • To send you occasional updates, only if you subscribed. You can unsubscribe at any time.
  • To introduce you to my credit partner ComparaJá, only if you ticked the box to agree.

I use your data because you asked me to contact you, to prepare a mediation contract with you, or because you gave your consent.

Who sees it

  • Engel & Völkers Lisboa, the agency I work with, where your details are recorded in our client system.
  • ComparaJá, only with your consent, for financing.
  • A trusted colleague in another region of Portugal, only with your consent, when you ask me to connect you.
  • The services that run this website and its forms, Netlify, and WhatsApp when you message me there.

I never sell your data. When a sale or purchase goes ahead, Portuguese law requires me to identify sellers and buyers, and that information is kept as the law requires.

How long I keep it

As long as we are in contact about selling or buying, and up to two years after our last contact, unless the law requires longer. Newsletter subscribers stay on the list until they unsubscribe.

Your rights

You can ask me at any time to see, correct or delete your data, to stop using it, or to withdraw your consent. Just send me an email. You can also file a complaint with the Portuguese data protection authority, CNPD, at www.cnpd.pt.

Cookies and visitor statistics

This website does not use tracking or advertising cookies. The fonts are loaded from Google Fonts, which means your browser connects to Google's servers to show them. To understand how many people visit and which pages they read, I use Cloudflare Web Analytics. It counts visits without cookies and without collecting personal data, so it cannot identify you. To save you typing, your name, phone number and email are remembered only in your own browser, on your device, so the other forms are filled in for you. Nothing is sent until you press send.
